title: Chapter 61 — Job-Site Coordination & Delivery for Construction
intro: Construction-calendar fluency, site-delivery craft, and the coordination that makes you infrastructure.

sections.title: Construction Calendar Fluency
sections.content:
Construction projects move in phases. The appliance delivery must align with the right phase — after cabinetry is installed but before the countertops go in, or after everything is complete depending on the builder's preference.

Learn the language: rough-in, framing, drywall, cabinetry, countertops, finish. Know which phase requires which measurements. Gas lines and electrical circuits are roughed in early — you need to provide specs before framing is closed up.

sections.title: Site Delivery Craft
sections.content:
Construction site delivery is different from residential delivery. The site may not have a finished floor, the doorways may not have trim, and there may not be power connected yet.

Coordinate delivery time with the site foreman, not just the builder. Confirm access — is the driveway poured? Can the truck get in? Where will the appliances be staged? Protect the appliances — if they are being staged before installation, they need to be wrapped and stored safely.

One damaged appliance on a construction site delays the entire project. The builder will not forgive it.

sections.title: Multi-Phase Coordination
sections.content:
Large projects may have 3-4 delivery phases. Rough-in specs first. Then the appliances that need to be in place before countertops. Then the rest after the finish work.

Create a delivery schedule tied to the construction timeline. Share it with the builder and update it as the schedule shifts — because it will shift. The rep who tracks the construction calendar and proactively adjusts delivery dates becomes irreplaceable.
